task.name.empty: The task name cannot be empty.
task.name.windows: The task name `{name}` does not work on Windows: the task name is the folder name. Use none of `< > : " | ? *`, and do not end with a space or a dot.
task.name.bad: The task name `{name}` cannot be used. No `/` or `\`, no `.` at the start, {limit} characters at most.
task.exists: Task `{task}` exists already. To go on with it, run `{command} task open {name} --session-id <session id>`.
task.missing: There is no task `{name}`. See which there are: `{command} task list --all`. To make one: `{command} task new {name} --kind <kind> --session-id <session id>`.
task.session.missing: There is no session `{session_id}`. Use the "current session id" from the rules at the top of this prompt, copied as written.
task.session.subagent: A subagent cannot open a task or switch tasks.
task.session.admin: This session is in admin mode and cannot work on a task. Ask the user to open another conversation, or to run `admin off` first.
task.closed: Task `{task}` is closed. To go on with it, run `{command} task open {name} --session-id <session id>`.
task.upgrade.down: The task is at the "{current}" tier and cannot change to "{wanted}". A tier only goes up, never down.
task.upgrade.same: The task is at the "{current}" tier already.
task.next.light: Read {task}/TASK.md first. Do the work, then write the result and the next step back into TASK.md.
task.next.medium: Read {task}/TASK.md first, then REQ.md, REQ/ and REF/. Write the requirement as you understand it into {task}/REQ.md and ask the user to look at it; when the requirement changes, change that file. Results go at the root of {task}/ (for example RCA.md, DESIGN.md). Append what you did, and why, to LOG.md. Update TASK.md before you stop.
task.next.full: Read {task}/TASK.md first, then REQ.md, REQ/ and REF/. Write the requirement as you understand it into {task}/REQ.md and ask the user to look at it; when the requirement changes, change that file. Write the steps into TODO.md. Update TASK.md before you stop, and append the decisions you made to LOG.md.
task.next.qa: Answer without asking first. Under "## Answer" in TASK.md write the answer, its source, and each command you ran with what it returned. Once TASK.md is saved, close the task in a step of its own (not beside the edit): `{command} task close --task {name}`. The user can open it again.
task.next.reopened: The task was closed and is open again as it was; this kind of task has no new round. To redo the work for a changed requirement, start a new task from this one: `{command} task fork <new task name> --from {name} --kind <kind> --session-id <session id>`.
task.next.switched: This session was on `{other}` before; that task is still open, not closed. To go back: `{command} task open {other_name} --session-id <session id>`.
task.waiting.plan: the plan waits for your approval
task.waiting.promote: the promote (write-back repo) waits for your approval
task.waiting.recover: the promote failed halfway and waits for you to recover
task.upgrade.done: Raised to the "{tier}" tier. Change the tier line in {task}/TASK.md to "{tier}".
task.upgrade.kind: A task of kind "{kind}" keeps its kind: only a Q&A task can become another kind. For other work, fork the task with the skill harness-task-fork.
task.upgrade.kind.done: It is now a "{kind}" task at the "{tier}" tier. Change the kind and tier lines in {task}/TASK.md to match.
task.upgrade.kind.hint: The kind is still Q&A. If this is now other work, run `{command} task upgrade --kind <kind>`: rca, design, dev, test, kb or other.
task.relay.reminder: In this round you wrote files in the task folder {task} but did not update {task}/TASK.md. Update it now: status, doing now, next step, decided. Change this one file only, then end. It is the handover file the next session reads.
task.inject.head: Task: {task} ({kind}, {tier} tier), round {round}. A new session reads {task}/TASK.md first, then what it points to; update it before you stop.
task.inject.scope: The edit tools can write this task folder only: the requirement goes in REQ.md; notes, RCA, design and read-only queries go at the root; code goes in {task}/DEV/ after the plan is approved (DEV/<repository>/ to promote, DEV/_manual/ when the user runs it by hand); REQ/ and REF/ hold the user's material and are read only. A target repository is written only with `{command} task promote`: --dry-run first, then the user approves in the terminal. Only the user can run approve-plan, approve-promote and recover. Do not clean up files with `rm`. The task folder is ignored by git, so search tools such as Glob and Grep do not find the files in it: read them by path with the file-reading tool, or use `ls` in the terminal.
task.inject.board: The task's page, where the user follows it (plan, TODO, log, changes, approvals): {url}. This is the task's URL: give it when the user asks for the link or the page of the task, and with the path whenever you point at a task file. Never open or request it yourself: the gate refuses.
rules.task.entry: When the user asks you to produce or change files (RCA, design, plan, development, tests, knowledge base changes), or mentions going on with, continuing or looking at an existing task (even just to ask how far it is), first open or pick up the task with the skill `harness-my-task`, then read, then act. For plain Q&A that writes nothing and touches no existing task, do not. Without a task you cannot call the reviewer; the mapper does not depend on a task, only on whether the user typed `/generic-mapreduce`. The files of a target repository are never changed directly.
gate.target.direct: `{repo}/{relative}` is in the working tree of the target repository {repo}. A target repository is never changed directly: only promote writes to it. Change `DEV/{repo}/{relative}` in the task folder, then write it back with `{command} task promote` (the user must approve). If the repository already has this file, fetch it first: `{command} task fetch {repo}/{relative}`. If there is no task yet, open one with the skill `harness-my-task`.
review.off: Independent checks are off for this task. They run only when the user switches them on, on the task page or with `[review]=n` in a prompt (n is the number of passes needed in a row). Do not switch them on yourself, and do not call the reviewer.
review.nothing: Task {task} has no work to check yet. Write the work first (under DEV/ if it is promoted, at the root of the task folder if not), then run `{command} task review start`.
review.enough: The passes needed in a row ({n}) are reached: no more checks are needed. A new check is needed only when the work changes.
review.limit: The checks are used up: checks done: {used}; limit: {limit}; and there are not enough passes yet. Stop: do not change or check any more. Tell the user where the last problems are (the newest verdict.md under {task}/REVIEW/) and ask the user to decide: run `{command} task review extend --checks <number>` in their own terminal for more checks, or `{command} task review waive` to stop checking. You cannot run these two commands.
review.start.next: Now call the subagent `{agent}`. The call message is one sentence only: "Check the review package {package}". Do not write your reasoning, your conclusion, or what you think is fine. After it answers, the verdict is saved as verdict.md in the same folder by itself. Then run `{command} task review status` for the next step.
review.next.waived: The user has waived the checks: no more are needed.
review.next.done: The passes needed in a row ({n}) are reached. You may go on.
review.next.more: Passes still needed: {left} (needed in a row: {n}, each with a new reviewer). Run `{command} task review start`.
review.next.fix: The last check did not pass. Read {verdict} and fix the work as it says; then run `{command} task review start` to check again. Passes still needed: {left}.
review.package.title: # Review package: {name}, check {number}
review.package.first: This is check 1. Do a full check.
review.package.later: This is check {ordinal} (the 2nd or later). Still do a full check, but **report only what affects correctness**: wording, format, naming and nicer ways to write something are not reported.
review.package.unconfirmed: The confirmation line of {req} is not filled in yet. Only the user can change that line; the author cannot. **It is not a problem: do not give FAIL for it.** Treat the requirement as "to be confirmed": check against what REQ.md says now.
review.package.diff:
## Diff

The diff between the work and main is in {path}. Read it first; for a large file read only the diff and the lines around it. The work is not in a git repository: do not use git diff.
review.package.evidence:
## The runs the task cites

The work cites saved runs as `[E<n>]`: each is in the file named, with the command and its output as saved, and what let it through. Where the command is a read of an outside system (a query), run it yourself on the same environment and compare with the saved output: a read needs no leave, and a result that differs is a finding (name the results file and the line of the run). A write or a procedure is refused to you by the gate: do not ask for it, judge it by the saved output. Never type a password: the way in is on the process.
review.package.previous:
## The problems of the last check

The last check did not pass; its text is in {path}. First confirm, one by one, whether each is fixed, then do the full check.
review.package.output:
## How to answer

The first line is `VERDICT: PASS` or `VERDICT: FAIL`. After it, one line per finding: `- <file>:<line> <what does not match> | basis: <source>`; when the items of REQ.md are numbered, the source names the item. A finding with no file and line does not count.
review.extend.screen: Task {task}: checks done: {used}; limit: {limit}; last verdict: {last}. More checks to give: {checks}.
review.extend.next: Tell the agent it may go on checking.
review.waive.screen: Task {task}: passes needed in a row: {n}; passes so far: {passes}; checks done: {used}; last verdict: {last}. After the waiver this version of the work can be promoted with no more checks. If the work changes, the waiver ends.
review.waive.ask: To stop checking and let this version through
review.waive.next: Tell the agent the checks are waived and it may run task promote --dry-run.
review.waive.unneeded: No waiver is needed: checks are off for this task, or it has enough passes already.
review.waive.changed: The work changed while you were confirming. Run this command again.
review.handoff_open: Task {task} is handed to the user ({what} {env}): their result is not back, so there is nothing to check yet. No check was used. When the user brings it back (in the chat, or on the task page: then the newest folder of `INBOX/<environment>/` holds it), record it with `{command} task run record --env <environment> --given-file <file> --ran-file <file> --evidence "<picture>::<what it shows>"` (it saves the commands, the words and the pictures in RUNS/<environment>/ and clears the handoff), then run `{command} task review start`.
review.runs_missing: {req} has items shown by a run the user does before the promote, and there is no result yet in {folders}. No check was used. Do this now: run `{command} task handoff run --env <environment> --what "<what to run>"` yourself (it is your command; it marks the task as waiting for the user's run), tell the user what to run, and stop. When the user sends the result back (in the chat, or on the task page: `INBOX/<environment>/`): record it with `{command} task run record --env <environment> --given-file <file> --ran-file <file> --evidence "<picture>::<what it shows>"`, then run `{command} task review start`.
review.runs_marked: {req} has items shown by a run the user does before the promote, and there is no result yet in `{folder}`. No check was used. The harness marked the task as waiting for the user's run in {env}: {what}. Tell the user what to run and what to send back (the output, the commands, a screenshot), then stop. When the user sends the result (in the chat, or on the task page: `INBOX/{env}/`): record it with `{command} task run record --env {env} --given-file <file> --ran-file <file> --evidence "<picture>::<what it shows>"`, check it against every R item of REQ.md (ask again with `{command} task handoff run` for what is missing), then run `{command} task review start`.
review.package.items:
## What this check judges

The items of "Done when" in {req} are numbered. `[T…]`: shown by the task files; check them. `[R…]`: shown by a run the user did before the promote; judge them only by the result saved in {runs}. `[A…]` ({after}): shown after the promote, in the environments; **do not judge them, they are not findings.** Name the item in the basis of each finding (`| basis: REQ.md T2`). A script drops a finding whose basis is only `[A…]` items, or whose file and line do not exist.
review.package.given_back:
## The last check was not counted

In {path} no finding was left after the script dropped these (the check was given back). Do the full check; name a file and line that exist, and the item, for each finding.
review.package.dropped: The script dropped these findings of that check:
review.dropped.after: only items checked after the promote ({items})
review.dismiss.none: Task {task} has no check to dismiss ({round}): only a finished check of this round that did not pass, and is not dismissed yet, can be.
review.dismiss.screen: Task {task}: check {round}, verdict {verdict}. Its answer is in {path}. Dismiss it only when you judge the reviewer was wrong: it then counts neither as a check used nor as a FAIL, and the next check starts afresh.
review.dismiss.log: - {day}: the user dismissed check {round} ({verdict}): they judged the reviewer was wrong. It does not count.
review.dismiss.next: Tell the agent the check was dismissed: it runs `{command} task review start` again, without changing the work for that check's findings.
task.handoff.run_what: Say what the user is to run with --what: one line, up to {limit} characters.
task.handoff.next.run: The board now says the task waits for the user's run in {env}, and no check can start. Tell the user exactly what to run and what to send back (the output, the commands, a screenshot), then stop. When they bring it back (in the chat, or on the task page: the newest folder of `INBOX/{env}/`): record it with `{command} task run record --env {env} --given-file <file> --ran-file <file> --evidence "<picture>::<what it shows>"`; it saves them under {folder} and clears the handoff. Then go on.
task.handoff.cleared.run: The mark is gone. Save what the user gave, as it is, under {folder}. Then check it against each R item of REQ.md, one by one: when something an item asks for is missing (a count, a log), do not start a check, since the reviewer will fail it; ask for the rest with `{command} task handoff run` again. Only when every R item is covered, run `{command} task review start`.
autorun.why.handoff: it waits for a run the user does outside the harness
desk.hint.review-dismiss: The newest check did not pass. If you judge the reviewer was wrong, dismiss it: it no longer counts as a check used or as a FAIL. LOG.md and the task record say so.
desk.review.invalid: no finding left (counted: the free ones are used)
review.promote.refused: It cannot be promoted yet: independent check passes needed in a row: {n}; so far: {passes}.
review.call.other: With a task, only the subagent `{agent}` can be called (you called: {called}), and a check must be started first.
review.call.no_round: Before calling `{agent}`, run `{command} task review start`: it saves this version of the work and writes the review package. Then call it.
review.stop: Independent checks are on for task {task}, and this version of the work does not have enough passes yet. {next}
review.inject: Independent checks: passes needed in a row: {n}; passes so far: {passes}; checks done: {used}; limit: {limit}. When the work is written: `{command} task review start`, then call `{agent}`; if it does not pass, fix it as verdict.md says and check again; only with enough passes can you run `task promote --dry-run`.
review.start.context: The review package of this check: {package}. Read it first and check as it says. Your answer is saved as written, as verdict.md in the same folder.
rules.task.open_list: Tasks that are not closed ({count}): {names}. When the user means one of them, first run `{command} task open <task name> --session-id <current session id>` to pick it up, then read its TASK.md. If you read or write without picking it up, the rules do not apply. A look at a server or at files is a new Q&A task, even when one of these has a like name or an attached file is from one: pick one up only when the user names it.
task.inject.req: When what the user asks in this prompt differs from {task}/REQ.md, or adds a new condition: change REQ.md first and add a line to its change record, then touch the work. A direct instruction ("write it as ...", "add a sentence ...") is a change of the requirement too. An independent check goes by REQ.md only.
rules.session: Current session id: {session_id}. Use it as written for --session-id of `{command} task new` and `task open`. When a tool call is refused, do the next step the refusal gives; do not look for another way around.
rules.review.no_task: The user wrote `[review]={n}` in this prompt: an independent check is wanted. A check needs a task. First open or pick up a task with the skill `harness-my-task` (the light tier is enough for something simple); n is carried into the task by itself.
rules.subagent.no_task: This session has no task, so it cannot call a subagent (you called: {called}). Do the work yourself. For an independent check: first open or pick up a task with the skill `harness-my-task`; `{agent}` can be called only after the user writes `[review]=n`.
rules.subagent.admin: Admin mode allows no subagent (you called: {called}). Do the work yourself.
mapreduce.call.not_asked: The subagent `{agent}` cannot be called: it is available only after the user types `/{skill}` (and again after it is used up or out of date). You cannot switch it on yourself. Do the work yourself; if running in parallel seems worth it, tell the user they can type `/{skill}`, and say roughly how much more it costs.
mapreduce.call.limit: The {limit} calls of `{agent}` for this `/{skill}` are used up: no more are sent. Finish with the summaries you have; if they really are not enough, tell the user which parts are missing, and the user decides whether to type `/{skill}` once more.
mapreduce.start.context: You are a mapper: read only, change no file, run no command. Do only the part the call message gives you. When you have read it, hand in a summary only: conclusions first, each with its source (file path and line number), and at the end "not found" and "not sure". Do not paste long passages.
rules.admin:
Admin mode: on (the user approved it in their own terminal). This session is for extending and debugging the harness: read the skill harness-admin first.
You may change the files of the harness, guardrail files included. Still closed: {locked} (read only), files the CLI writes (reports, a task's `.task/` and so on), `.git`, target repositories.
You cannot call a subagent or open a task. Only the user can run the approval commands (approve-plan, approve-promote, recover, approve-command, admin on, task review extend, task review waive). The rules for git write commands and dangerous commands stay the same.
After changing `.harness/engine/`, a policy or the hook configuration, run `{command} doctor` and the tests, and hand over to the user only when both pass. When a tool call is refused, do the next step the refusal gives.
Current session id: {session_id}. When you are done, remind the user to run `{command} admin off --session-id {session_id}`.
task.waiting.review: the checks are used up and wait for your decision
task.waiting.go-req: the requirement is confirmed: tell the agent to go on
task.waiting.go-plan: the plan is approved: tell the agent to go on
task.waiting.go-promote: the promote (write-back repo) is approved: tell the agent to run it
task.waiting.go-recover: the repositories are put back: tell the agent to try again
task.waiting.go-review: the checks are decided: tell the agent to go on
desk.wait.go-recover: The agent does not know yet: nothing tells it. In VS Code, send it a message, for example:
desk.wait.go-review: The agent does not know yet: nothing tells it. In VS Code, send it a message, for example:
desk.go.recover: The repositories are put back. Try the promote (write-back repo) again.
desk.go.review: The checks are decided. Go on.
task.waiting.autorun: autorun stopped and waits for you
autorun.inject: Autorun is on (pushed on {step}/{limit} times so far): work down {task}/TODO.md, tick each step when it is done, write decisions and reasons into LOG.md, and do not stop to ask the user. No promote on the way. When you cannot go on, run `{command} task autorun off --reason "<why>"`, then stop.
autorun.next.step: Go on with the next unticked step in {task}/TODO.md: "{step}" ({left} steps left). When it is done, tick it in TODO.md, update TASK.md, and write your decisions and reasons into LOG.md. Do not ask the user, and do not promote. When you cannot go on (missing information, a trade-off the plan does not cover, a refusal), run `{command} task autorun off --reason "<why>"`, then stop.
autorun.next.review: Every step is ticked, and the independent check has not passed yet. {next}
autorun.next.promote: Every step is ticked and the check has passed. Run `{command} task promote --dry-run`, put the link to PROMOTE-PLAN.diff in your answer, then stop and wait for the user to approve. Do not run promote without --dry-run.
autorun.cannot: Autorun cannot be switched on now:
autorun.need.plan: There is no plan yet. Let the agent write PLAN.md first, then run `{command} task approve-plan --task {name}`.
autorun.need.approval: The plan is not approved, or it changed after the approval. Run `{command} task approve-plan --task {name}` first.
autorun.need.todo: {task}/TODO.md has no unticked step. Let the agent break the work into `- [ ] step` lines there first (for a light or medium task, run `{command} task upgrade --tier full` first).
autorun.need.review: Independent checks are off for this task. With nobody watching there must be a reviewer: first switch on Independent review on the task page.
autorun.need.round: This round was promoted already, or the promote (write-back repo) failed halfway. To do more, open a new round or recover first.
autorun.changed: While you were confirming, the plan or the steps changed, or a condition no longer holds. Not switched on. Run it again to see the new content.
autorun.screen.head: Task {task} (round {round}): switch autorun on (beta). The agent works down TODO.md and no longer stops after each step to wait for you.
autorun.screen.limits: When it stops: pushed on {steps} times; {minutes} minutes passed; refusals by the gate: {denies}; several rounds with no progress; the independent check ({n} in a row) has used its checks ({checks}) without a pass; the plan changes; the agent says it cannot go on.
autorun.screen.scope: Scope: it can write {task}/ only, and the plan is the version you approved. git and the target repositories stay out of reach as before.
autorun.screen.end: When it is done: it makes the promote plan and stops. The promote (write-back repo) still needs your approve-promote. You can switch it off any time with `task autorun off`.
autorun.screen.question: To switch autorun on
autorun.on.next: Autorun is on. Go back to the session of the task and send "start". After that you need not watch; for progress: `{command} task list --watch` or `{command} task autorun status`.
autorun.off.reason: Switching autorun off needs a reason: `{command} task autorun off --reason "<why it cannot go on>"`. The user reads it to see where it got stuck.
autorun.off.next.person: Autorun is off. The next time the agent stops, it is not pushed on any more.
autorun.off.next.agent: Autorun is off, and the reason is recorded. Stop now, and tell the user in a sentence or two where it got stuck and what they need to decide.
autorun.why.done: done: every step is ticked, the check passed, and the promote plan is made (or there is nothing to promote)
autorun.why.plan: the plan is no longer the approved version
autorun.why.review: the independent checks are used up without a pass
autorun.why.denied: refusals by the gate reached the limit
autorun.why.steps: the times pushed on reached the limit
autorun.why.agent: the agent said it cannot go on
task.pause.next: The task is paused: the board no longer says it waits for you, and this time does not count as waiting. To go on: `{command} task resume --task {name}`, or just send a prompt in its session.
task.pause.already: Task {name} is paused already. To go on: `{command} task resume --task {name}`.
task.offwork.next: Paused {count} task(s) for the night: the time aside is not counted as waiting. `{command} task onwork` takes them back.
task.offwork.left: Left as they are (the agent is at work, or autorun is on): {names}.
task.onwork.next: Took back {count} task(s): each goes on waiting from where it stood; the time aside is not counted.
task.onwork.kept: Still paused, as you paused them by hand: {names}.
task.resume.not_paused: Task {name} is not paused: nothing to resume.
insight.not_started: Task `{task}` has not started: there is no record to analyse.
insight.wait.commit: promoted, waiting for you to commit and close
insight.wait.reply: the agent stopped and waited for your reply
insight.wait.cancelled: you cancelled the agent; it waited for you
insight.wait.plan: waiting for you to approve the plan
insight.wait.promote: waiting for you to approve the promote (write-back repo)
insight.wait.review: the checks were used up, waiting for your decision
insight.wait.recover: waiting for you to recover the repository
insight.why.calls: It made {calls} tool calls in all
insight.why.part: Of that, "{part}" took {time} ({turns} turns, {calls} tool calls)
insight.finding.waiting: Waiting for you took {waiting}; the agent worked for {active}: waiting is {share} of the whole. The longest wait came after prompt {prompt}: {longest} ({reason}).
insight.finding.slow_prompt: The slowest was prompt {prompt}: {time}, {share} of the working time. {why}.
insight.finding.time_split: Of the working time, the biggest part is "{part}": {time}, {share}.
insight.finding.approval: Tools stopped to wait for your confirmation click for {time} in all, {share} of the working time.
insight.finding.dear_prompt: The prompt with the most usage is prompt {prompt}: {aiu} Credits, {share} of the total. Turns: {turns}. It ended with {context} tokens of context.
insight.finding.review: Independent checks done: {checks}; not passed: {fails}. The prompts of the checks took {time} ({share} of the working time) and {aiu_share} of the usage; the reviewers used {tokens} tokens in all.
insight.finding.context: The context grew from {first} tokens to {largest} tokens ({times} times). The larger the context, the more each later turn costs.
insight.finding.compacted: Copilot compacted the context {times} time(s), in prompt {prompts}: it replaced the earlier messages with a summary (last time {before} → {after} tokens). Details from before that point may be gone. If the agent went wrong after it, that may be why.
insight.finding.tool_results: Tool {tool}: {calls} calls. Its results came to {tokens} tokens, all of which went into the context.
insight.finding.slow_tool: The tool that took the most time is {tool}: {calls} calls, {time} in all, {longest} for the longest.
insight.finding.refused: Actions the hook refused: {denied}. Times it blocked Stop: {blocks}. After each refusal the agent has to try another way.
insight.finding.no_usage: For some sessions Copilot's session record was not found: that part has times only, no usage.
insight.finding.paused: You paused this task for {time} (`task pause`). That time does not count as "waiting for you".
report.title: Task analysis: {name}
report.subtitle: {kind} · {tier} tier · {status} · {start} to {end} · made at {as_of}
report.now: Waiting for you now: {text}. Waited {time} so far. This stretch is counted in "waiting for you" below, up to the time this page was made.
report.empty: No session record was found for this task. The logs may have been pruned, or the task has not had a prompt yet.
report.context.note: Each dot is the context at the end of one prompt. From {first} to {largest} at most.

gate.write.no_path: The gate cannot read which file `{tool}` would write, so the call is refused. Do not get around this with a terminal command. Tell the user the tool name, and that `{command} doctor` lists it.
gate.guardrail.file: `{relative}` is a guardrail file ({pattern}). It cannot be changed. Do not change it, and do not get around this with a terminal command. If it must change, stop and tell the user what to change: the user changes it, or switches admin mode on for a session (`harness admin on`).
gate.admin.file: `{relative}` cannot be changed in admin mode either ({pattern}): session state, approval records and logs live here, read only. Do not get around this with a terminal command. If it really must be cleaned or repaired, stop and tell the user: the user does it.
gate.admin.terminal: This terminal command would change files that stay closed in admin mode too ({why}), such as the session state, approval records and logs in `.harness/runtime/`. Do not retry with another command. If it really must be cleaned or repaired, stop and tell the user: the user does it.
gate.guardrail.terminal: This terminal command would change a guardrail file ({why}). Guardrail files cannot be changed. Do not retry with another command. If it must change, stop and tell the user what to change: the user changes it, or switches admin mode on for a session (`harness admin on`).
gate.git_folder.file: `{shown}` is inside a `.git` folder. `.git` is never changed directly: that breaks the history and the settings of the repository. Do not change it, and do not get around this with a terminal command. If you need a commit or another branch, stop and tell the user.
gate.git_folder.terminal: This terminal command would directly change a `.git` folder or a path a target repository refuses ({why}). Do not retry with another command. If it is needed, stop and tell the user what to do: the user does it.
gate.target.refused: `{repo}/{relative}` is a path the target repository {repo} refuses ({pattern}, see refused_paths in target.json). It is never changed. If it must change, stop and tell the user: the user changes it.
gate.target.terminal: This terminal command would directly change files in the working tree of a target repository ({why}). Only promote writes to a target repository. Do not retry with another command. Fetch the file into the task's DEV/, change it there, then write it back with promote.
gate.task.plan_req: `{relative}` is under the task's `DEV/`. The requirement of the task changed after the user approved the plan, so `DEV/` is closed again. Check that {task}/PLAN.md still fits the requirement (change it if not), then stop and tell the user to read the requirement and the plan again, confirm the requirement and run `{command} task approve-plan` (or press the buttons on the task's page). Go on when the user says it is approved. Meanwhile write only notes, RCA, design and read-only queries, at the root of {task}/: code waits, code run by hand too.
desk.req.changed: The requirement changed after you confirmed it or after you approved the plan. Read it again: confirm it, and approve the plan again.
gate.task.plan_first: `{relative}` is under the task's `DEV/`. `DEV/` can be written only after the user approves the plan (it is not approved now, or it changed after the approval). Write [PLAN.md]({task}/PLAN.md), then stop and ask the user to run `{command} task approve-plan` in their own terminal. Go on when the user says it is approved. Code the user runs by hand (on a server, in a database) waits for the plan too: it goes in `DEV/_manual/<path>`. Only notes, RCA, design and read-only queries go at the root of `{task}/` without approval.
gate.task.outside: Task {task} is open: you may write only inside the task folder `{task}/`, and you tried to write `{relative}`. Notes, RCA, design and read-only queries go at the root of the task folder; code goes under `{task}/DEV/` once the plan is approved: `DEV/<repository>/<path>` to promote, `DEV/_manual/<path>` when the user runs it by hand.
gate.task.person_files: `{relative}` is in `REQ/`, `REF/` or `INBOX/` of task {task}. Those hold what the user gave and are read only. Write notes and results at the root of the task folder `{task}/`.
gate.board.request: Refused: this asks the board server on port {port}, and its buttons are the user's. Do not call it. If something on the board should change, tell the user.
gate.terminal.denied: This terminal command is refused: {why}. Do not retry with a command of the same kind. If it is needed, stop and tell the user why: the user runs it.
gate.external.subagent:
You are the {agent} subagent: you may only read outside systems. This {verb} on {place} is refused, whatever the main agent was allowed: the user's leave is not yours. Command: {call}
Do not retry it. Judge by the saved output, and say in your answer what you could not check.
gate.external.unlinked: Refused: this writes {ref} of {system}, and this task does not name it. A task writes only the items it is linked to. If the user means this one: {step} Command: {call}
gate.external.denied:
This call to {place} is refused: the kind {verb} is not allowed there. Command: {call}
Do not retry it, and do not look for another way to the same result. If it is needed, stop and tell the user why: the user decides.
gate.external.human:
An agent cannot run this call to {place} directly: its kind is {verb}, and the rules say a person does it. Command: {call}
Give the user the whole command and what it is for. In a task, `{command} task handoff run{handoff_env} --what "<what to run>"` hands it over and keeps the result. Do not run it another way.
gate.external.task:
This call to {place} is of kind {verb}. It is allowed only in a task whose plan the user approved. Command: {call}
Open or continue a task with the skill `harness-my-task`, get `PLAN.md` approved, then run it.
gate.external.outbox:
This call to {place} is {verb} that leaves this repository, so the user approves it first. Command: {call}
{where} Tell the user in one or two sentences what the command does and why. Then run `{command} wait --approval {code}`: it waits here with no model call, up to 9 minutes, and returns at once when the user decides on the task page (the card of this call shows the command; the user reads it, types the code {code} and presses {@desk.outbox.approve}). When it says approved, run exactly the same command once more within {minutes} minutes. When it says not approved, read the reason in it and do what it says. If it ends with no answer, end your turn: say which call waits and that the user can approve it later; the board wakes you when they do. A changed command needs a new approval. Do not run approve-action yourself, and do not reach the same result another way (another program, a script, the service's web address).
wait.next.timeout: No match in {seconds} seconds. The last output is in {out}. A job that is still running is waited for with another `harness wait` (one call at a time, each under 10 minutes: VS Code hands a longer terminal call back and you would have to poll it); tell the user what the last output says if it looks wrong. Do not start the job again.
wait.next.matched: The output matched. The last output is in {out}: record it with `task run record --run-by agent` and cite the number.
wait.round_slow: (the command gave no answer in {seconds} seconds)
wait.out_place: --out must be a file inside a task folder ({folder}/<task>/...), as RUNS/DEV/wait-job.txt is.
wait.not_read: The command of --run is a {verb} on {system}. Only a read may be run again and again; start a job with its own command, then wait with a query.
wait.not_listed: The command of --run reaches no outside system the company listed (tools.company.json or tools.override.json). `harness wait` runs a read of a listed system only; it is not a way to run anything else.
wait.pattern: --until is not a pattern that compiles: {pattern!r}: {error}.
gate.external.outbox_nodraft: No task is open, so there is no draft file.
gate.external.autorun:
This call to {place} is {verb} that the user must approve or run, and autorun is on: nobody is there to approve it now. Command: {call}
Write in LOG.md what you wanted to run and why, run `{command} task autorun off --reason "needs the user: {system}"`, and stop.
gate.external.approved:
The user approved these outside calls. Each may run once, in this session, spelled exactly as here, within the time limit:
{calls}
outbox.draft.title: # Outbox {code}: {place}
outbox.draft.unnamed: No verb of the system is in the command: counted as a write
outbox.draft.how: To approve: on the task page, open the card of this call, read the command, type the code {code} and press {@desk.outbox.approve}. The same command then runs once, in the same session, within {minutes} minutes. Only the harness writes this file.

gate.action.none: No call to an outside system is waiting for approval (within {minutes} minutes). Let the agent run the command first, and come back after it is refused.

target.unknown: There is no target repository called `{name}`. Known repositories: {known}.

target.not_git: The path of repository {name} is not a git repository: {location}

queue.blocked: The repository is on branch `{current}` now: task {task} wrote it back, and the files are not committed yet. queue.next.held: The repository is on branch {branch}, promoted by task {task}, with {files} uncommitted files. Check and commit in the repository; the tasks in the queue can promote only after that.
queue.next.dirty: The repository has {files} uncommitted files that no harness task wrote back. Commit, stash or discard them first.
queue.next.ready: The repository is clean. Task {task} is approved, but its dry run may be out of date now: tell its agent to run `harness task promote --dry-run` again, then `harness task promote`.
queue.next.asked: The repository is clean. The promote plan of task {task} is waiting for your approval: `{command} task approve-promote --task {task}`.
queue.next.working: The repository is clean. Task {task} is still in progress and has no promote plan.

refs.short: `{term}` has fewer than {minimum} characters and would match almost everything. Give a longer name, or `table.column`.
refs.no_terms: Give at least one name to look for.
refs.note.committed: Only the committed base branch of each repository is searched (what `task fetch` reads). Uncommitted files, branches, and names built from pieces at run time (dynamic SQL, string concatenation) are not seen.
refs.note.truncated: {name}: more than {limit} lines matched; only the first ones were read. Search a longer or more exact name.
refs.note.no_branch: {name} has no local branch `{base_ref}`; it was not searched.

skill.no_frontmatter: SKILL.md has no frontmatter (the block between two `---` lines at the top).
skill.name.folder: `name` is `{name}` but the folder is `{folder}`. They must be the same.
skill.name.form: `name` may hold lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only, at most 64 characters.
skill.name.prefix: `name` has none of the prefixes {prefixes}. That is fine for a third-party skill; a skill of your own needs one.
skill.prefix.form: `skill_prefix` in user.override.json is `{value}`: it must be lowercase letters and digits only (for example `acme`). It is not used.

skill.desc.missing: `description` is missing. Copilot picks a skill by its description alone.
skill.desc.wide: `description` has {count} characters. All descriptions share one budget in the context window: keep it under {limit}, short and full of the words a user would say.
skill.desc.when: `description` does not say when to use the skill (`Use when ...`). Copilot picks a skill by its description alone.
skill.specific.missing: `specificTo` is missing: `generic`, or the name of the domain.
skill.specific.domain: `specificTo` is `{actual}`, but the name says the domain is `{expected}`.
skill.body.long: SKILL.md has {count} lines, more than {maximum}. Move detail into references/.
skill.body.big: SKILL.md has {count} lines. Past {limit}, move detail into references/ and link it.
skill.link: The link `{link}` leads to no file.
skill.gotchas: There is no `## Gotchas` section. Write down each trap the agent fell into; it is the most useful part of a skill.
skill.claude: It mentions `.claude/`. This harness is for Copilot; do not tie a skill to another tool.
skill.secret: It looks like it holds a secret ({what}). Do not keep credentials in a skill.
skill.orphan: {path} is in the skill folder, but no text of the skill names it. Copilot opens a file only when a link points at it.

skill.next.errors: Fix the errors first; a warning is advice.

doctor.standards.incomplete: Rules of {file} that lack a field ({fields}): {titles}. The check needs `Applies to` and `Rule`.
fetch.spec: `{spec}` must be `<repository>/<path inside the repository>`, for example repo_b/src/a.sql.
fetch.no_branch: Repository {name} has no local branch `{base_ref}`. Prepare it in that repository first, and run `doctor` to check.
fetch.no_file: `{relative}` is not on {base_ref} ({commit}) of repository {name}. A new file needs no fetch: create it under DEV/.

fetch.too_many: {count} files in one copy; the limit is {limit}. Copy only the files this task needs.

output.refused: {label} `{name}` is a path that cannot be promoted ({pattern} of {repo}). Take it out of the results.

task.step.plan: Read REQ/, REF/ and the knowledge base. To change a target repository, or to write code the user runs by hand (on a server, in a database): write the plan to {plan} (which files change, how, and how to accept the result), then stop, give the user the link [PLAN.md]({plan}), and ask the user to run `{command} task approve-plan` in their own terminal; {dev}/ cannot be written before the approval. Work that stays in the task (RCA, design, notes, read-only queries) needs no plan: write it at the root of {task}/. {finish} If the change renames or removes something other code may use (a table, a column, a procedure, a job), run the skill generic-impact-analysis before you write the plan.
task.step.page: The user reads the plan on the task's page: {url}. Give that address with the link.
task.step.approve: The user has not approved the plan yet (or it, or the requirement, changed after the approval). Give the user the link [PLAN.md]({plan}) and ask the user to run `{command} task approve-plan` in their own terminal. {dev}/ cannot be written before the approval; meanwhile write only notes, RCA, design and read-only queries, at the root of {task}/.
task.step.handoff: The task waits for the user ({env}: {what}). Do not start a check or a promote that needs it. When the user brings the result (in the chat, or on the task page: `INBOX/{env}/`): record it with `{command} task run record --env {env} ...` (a test task: `task test record`), which clears the handoff, then go on.
task.step.test_agent: The user let the agent run these environments itself: {envs}. Run the steps of the guide there in the terminal (the gate judges each call), save what came back whole in TEST/given.txt and the commands in TEST/ran.txt, judge each criterion, then `{command} task test record --env <env> --run-by agent ...`. The other environments are handed over to the user as before.
task.step.approved: The plan is approved. Code to promote to a target repository goes under {dev}/<repository>/<path>; code the user runs by hand goes under {dev}/_manual/<path> and is never promoted; notes, RCA, design and read-only queries go at the root of {task}/.
task.step.fetch: To change a file the repository already has, fetch it first with `task fetch <repository>/<path>`; a file in no repository that the user runs by hand: `task fetch _manual/<path> --from <file>`. When done, run `task diff`, then `task promote --dry-run` (nothing under DEV/_manual/ is promoted: hand its run over with `task handoff run`).
task.step.close: {finish} If the task taught something a future agent would miss, or `LOG.md` notes knowledge base cards that are wrong, stale or missing (not a defect of the harness or the toolkit: tell the user about those), name them in two or three lines and ask the user whether to run the skill generic-capture-knowledge; do not run it unasked.
task.step.standards: The company has code standards plugged in ({file}). If this task changed code, ask the user whether to run the skill generic-code-standards before `task diff`; do not run it unasked.
task.step.then: Run this command again when the user says it is approved.

kb.domain.version: domain.yaml: schema_version is {found}; this harness reads {wanted}.
kb.domain.name: domain.yaml says domain `{found}`, but the folder is `{folder}`.

kb.domain.file_missing: domain.yaml files.{name} points at `{path}`, which is not there.

kb.domain.no_architecture: There is no architecture.md: the first file an agent reads.
kb.domain.architecture_long: architecture.md has more than {limit} lines. It is read first by every task: keep it short and link to the cards.
kb.object.twice: id `{id}` is on line {first} and again on line {line}.
kb.object.sources: `{id}` has no sources [{{path, sha}}]: `kb stale` cannot tell when it goes out of date.
kb.object.source_missing: `{id}`: `source_missing` must be an object with `seen_in` (where the object was seen running).
kb.object.gap_level: `{id}` has no source: its level should be `unknown` (or `conflict`).
kb.object.card_file: `{id}`: card `{card}` points at a file that is not there.
kb.object.no_anchor: `{id}`: card `{card}` names a file but no section (`file#{id}`): an agent must read the whole file.
kb.object.anchor: `{id}`: card `{card}` names a section that is not a heading of that file.
kb.object.card_long: `{id}`: its card section has {lines} lines (more than {limit}). A card longer than the code is not worth reading.
kb.local_path: {file} holds a path of one computer (`{found}`). Write `<repo>/<path inside it>` instead.
kb.check.ok: The knowledge base is in the standard form.
kb.check.errors: Fix the errors; warnings are advice. The form is in .harness/contracts/kb/README.md.
kb.stale.next: The cards of `changed` and `gone` were written from source that changed since. Before relying on one, read its source (`--diff` shows only what changed); tell the user which cards are out of date, and offer to refresh them (`generic-kb-refresh`) in a `kb` task.
kb.stale.fresh: No source of this domain changed since it was learned (objects without a sha cannot be told: see `unstamped`).
kb.stale.unreadable: git could not read some repositories (`unreadable_repos`): their cards are not judged. Check the repository and its base branch (`target show --repo <name>`).
kb.stale.no_diff: git no longer has the version the card was written from: read the source as it is now.
kb.stamp.not_dev: kb stamp writes only inside the DEV/ of a task (.workspace/sandbox/tasks/<task>/DEV/...): {folder}. Fetch the domain into a kb task first.
kb.stamp.next: The sources of these objects now count from the base branch as it is. Stamp only cards you checked against the change. Then `kb check --path <folder>`, and hand over through the promote.
kb.stamp.nothing: Every source already has the sha of the base branch: nothing to stamp.
kbmap.no_branch: It has no branch `{branch}`: nothing to map.
kbmap.no_repos: No target repository is set up. Run `target list`.
kbmap.no_toolkit: No toolkit: the knowledge base has no toolkit/toolkit.json for this repository. A toolkit is made for your own code with /generic-kb-toolkit-design and /generic-kb-toolkit-build (contract: .harness/contracts/kb/map.md). Until then, learn the repository by reading its folders.
kbmap.toolkit_bad: The toolkit in {folder} cannot be used: {problem}
kbmap.trial_outside: --toolkit must be a folder inside a task (.workspace/sandbox/tasks/<task>/...): {folder}. A toolkit in use is in the knowledge base's toolkit/.
kbmap.survey.next: Read a few `samples` of each kind that holds code (`task fetch` in a task), then design the toolkit: which files define which objects, what a use looks like, where work starts. Ask the user for uses they know. /generic-kb-toolkit-design leads it.
kbmap.next: Use `kb near <id>` for what one object uses and what uses it, and `kb split` for a first cut of the domains. `missing`: names used but defined nowhere in the repositories (deleted, or never committed); `obsolete_used`: retired code still in use. `dynamic` objects run code known only at run time: read them, or ask the user, before you rely on their uses. `unresolved`: names that fit no object (aliases, or a form the toolkit misreads). How right the map is: `kb audit` (generic-kb-toolkit-audit).
kbmap.next.facts: Check `facts` first: the toolkit does not yet find every use the person knows (or there is no facts.jsonl). Look also at `empty_files` and `failed_files`. Until they are right, the map misses uses: fix the toolkit (/generic-kb-toolkit-build).
kbmap.next.declared: Check `declared_uses` in the toolkit's declared.jsonl: `stale` lines name evidence no longer on the base branch near the line given (the code changed: read it again, fix the line or take it out); `not_in_map` lines name an id the map does not have; `bad_lines` miss a field. Until then those uses are left out of the map. `already_mapped`: the toolkit finds that use now, so its line can go.
kbmap.empty: The map found no object. Check the globs of toolkit.json against the files of the repository.
kbmap.none: There is no map yet. Run `harness kb map` first.
kbmap.near.none: No object in the map is called `{query}`. Run `harness kb map` again if the code changed.
kbmap.near.many: More than one object fits. Ask again with one of these ids.
kbmap.near.dynamic: This object runs SQL known only at run time: the uses listed may be incomplete.
kbmap.split.next: A first cut, by script: entry points joined by what they use. `shared` objects are used from many entry points and belong in shared/. Write the proposal for the user, with names they would use; the user confirms the domains once.
kbmap.split.one_big: One domain holds {size} objects: something used everywhere still joins them. Try a lower `--shared-min` (now {limit}).
kbstatus.audit.old: toolkit/audit.md is of another toolkit: the toolkit changed since it was audited.
kbstatus.next.targets: No code repository is set up. The setup guide on the board sets the target repositories up first.
kbstatus.next.kb_repo: The knowledge base is not a target repository yet, so no task can write it. The setup guide on the board sets it up (`harness target init-kb` and an entry in target.override.json).
kbstatus.next.toolkit: Next: the toolkit that lets a script read this code (once per code base). Offer `generic-kb-toolkit-design`; after the user approves the design, the user types `/generic-kb-toolkit-build`. The user will be asked for 5 to 10 uses they know ("job X runs procedure Y").
kbstatus.next.map: Next: run `harness kb map`. When facts are missing, or files failed, the toolkit is fixed first (the user types `/generic-kb-toolkit-build`).
kbstatus.next.audit: Next: measure how right the map is before learning from it. Offer `generic-kb-toolkit-audit`.
kbstatus.next.domains: Next: the domains. Offer `generic-kb-domains` (the user confirms the cut once). When the user already knows the domain to learn, go straight to `generic-kb-learn-plan` with its entry points.
kbstatus.next.plan: Next: learn `{domain}`. Offer `generic-kb-learn-plan`: it opens one task for the whole domain, plans its batches, and the user approves the plan once. Ask the user for the entry points, the scope, and any research note or runbook.
kbstatus.next.batch: Next: `{domain}` has {left} objects left in {batches} batches, and no task learns it. Offer `generic-kb-learn-plan`: it opens one task for the rest, from the plan the domain has.
kbstatus.map.empty: The toolkit found nothing in {repos}: another kind of code. Name the repositories the toolkit is for in `repos` of `toolkit.json`, or give that code a toolkit of its own.
kbstatus.next.task_plan: Next: the learn plan of `{domain}` waits in the task `{task}`. The user reads its PLAN.md and approves it in the terminal; then the batches are learned in that task.
kbstatus.next.task_batch: Next: go on learning `{domain}` in the task `{task}`: {left} objects left in {batches} batches. The user says "continue {task}" (a new chat every two or three batches keeps it sharp).
kbstatus.next.task_architecture: Next: every batch of `{domain}` is learned in the task `{task}`. Write its architecture there (`generic-kb-learn-synthesize`), then the whole domain is promoted once.
kbstatus.next.task_writeback: Next: `{domain}` is learned in the task `{task}` but not promoted. Run the diff and the promote dry-run there; the user approves the promote (write-back repo) in the terminal.
kbstatus.next.maintain: The knowledge base is built. From here it is kept true in daily work, and the user needs no command for it: when code changes, the agent sees which cards went stale and offers to fix them (`generic-kb-refresh`); when a task teaches something, the agent offers to write it in (`generic-capture-knowledge`); when someone answers a row of `requests.md`, the agent writes the answer in. To learn another domain: `generic-kb-learn-plan`.
kbstatus.stop: Before you stop: the knowledge base of this code is not built yet (step {step} of {of}). At the end of your answer, offer the next step to the user in one or two lines, and do not start it: {next} The user can turn this off: `"kb_offer": false` in .harness/policies/task.override.json.
kbaudit.type: No object of type {types} in the map.
kbaudit.sample.next: Read each object's code, blind: fetch its file and read it from `line` for `lines` lines; do not run `kb near` or look at the map for these objects first. Write one line per use you find into a JSON lines file in the task (form: `answer_form`; `{"from": id, "none": true}` for an object that uses nothing), with the line you saw it on. Then `kb audit --answers <file>`.
kbaudit.answers.line: line {line}: not a reading (needs `from`, and `to` or `none`)
kbaudit.score.pass: Every type is at or above the bar. Still look at `map_misses` and `map_only`: each is a use the map gets wrong. Write AUDIT.md and keep it with the toolkit.
kbaudit.score.fail: Below the bar, or lines not read. Check every difference at its line first: a reading that was wrong is fixed in the answers (say so in AUDIT.md), then score again. What is left is the map's: `map_misses` (the toolkit does not see a use) and `map_only` (the toolkit sees one that is not there). Fix the toolkit with /generic-kb-toolkit-build, with these as examples.
kbaudit.score.ambiguous: A reading names a short name that fits several objects (`ambiguous`: the same `schema.name` in two databases, say): it is not scored, and neither is the map's use of it. Look at the line, write the name in full as the code resolves it (the database of the file, or its `USE`), and score again.
kblearn.none: No object in the map is called `{query}`. Run `harness kb map` again if the code changed.
kblearn.many: More than one object is called `{query}`: {ids}. Give the id.
kblearn.order.next: The plan, by script. Write LEARN-PLAN.md from it for the user to approve: the batches in this order (each is learned in a task of its own; what a batch uses is in an earlier batch or earlier in the same one), `shared` for shared/, `stopped_at` and `outside` as boundaries, `missing` as requests for code, `dynamic` as requests for run-time values.
kblearn.flows.next: Paths by script: every use the entry point reaches, each on its shortest path. Write the Flows of architecture.md from them: an id for each step, an arrow between steps. `kb cardcheck` checks every flow line against the map.
kblearn.index.next: Lines added and stamped with the sha of the base branch. Next: `kb cardcheck --path` and `kb check --path` on the same folder.
kblearn.index.nothing: Every id is in the index already. To record that a card was checked again, use `kb stamp`.
kblearn.index.unstamped: Lines added, but some have no sha: `unknown_repos` are not set up here (`harness target list`), `gone` are not on the base branch. `kb stale` cannot follow them until they are stamped: set the repository up, or run `kb map` again, then `kb stamp`.
kblearn.check.nowhere: the map has no such use
kblearn.check.left_out: {id} ({file}): {field} leaves out {other}, which the map has
kblearn.check.flow: architecture.md line {line}: {left} and {right} are not linked in the map within {steps} steps
kblearn.check.no_cites: {id} ({file}): {lines} lines of code and no line cited. Cite the lines of each rule (`L120-L145`) so that it can be checked against the code
kblearn.check.few_cites: {id} ({file}): {lines} lines of code and no line cited
kblearn.check.cites_old: {id} ({file}): the card was stamped against older code, so its line numbers were not checked (`kb stale` lists it)
kblearn.check.cite_out: {id} ({file}): {cites} not in its code: {path} lines {low} to {high} on the base branch
kblearn.check.no_objects: No objects/ folder in {folder}: give the domain folder.
kblearn.check.bad: Fix the cards: a relation the map does not have is made up or under the wrong field; one the map has must be written. When the code is right and the map is wrong, fix the toolkit (`kb map`), not the card. `warning_list`: callers left out (allowed) and uses of objects whose SQL is known only at run time.
kblearn.check.ok: The relations of the cards and the flows agree with the map.
kbmap.gaps.inventory: The production list {file} cannot be read: {problem}
kbmap.gaps.no_ids: it holds no id (`type:name`, one per line, or a CSV with an `id` column)
kbmap.gaps.next: `in_production_not_in_repos`: production runs them but no repository has their code. Ask the user who can get the code (scripted from production, or the last version in git under `deleted`). Record each in the knowledge base with `source_missing` and level `unknown`. `in_repos_not_in_production`: not deployed, or retired without being moved to an obsolete folder: ask before calling them dead.
kbmap.gaps.next_no_inventory: These come from the repositories only: `missing` names are used but defined in no file; `deleted` shows where git had them and how to get the last version. What production runs that nothing uses is not seen here: ask the user to export the list of production objects with the toolkit's inventory query, then run `kb gaps --inventory <file>`.

desk.unknown: The board lists no task called `{name}`.
desk.fact.label: About this task
desk.actions.title: Waiting for you
desk.actions.paused.hint: You put this task aside. It is not counted as waiting. Take it up again when you are ready.
desk.wait.commit: The files are on the branch `{branch}`, not committed. The Changes tab has the commit message and the commands to commit it. The promote was your acceptance: the task closes by itself when nothing else waits.

desk.wait.cancelled: The last message was cancelled, so the agent stopped. Send it a new message here or in VS Code.
desk.wait.autorun: Read the reason in Task Record. Answer the agent in VS Code, or switch autorun on again.
desk.wait.go-req: The agent does not know yet: nothing tells it. In VS Code, send it a message, for example:
desk.wait.go-plan: The agent does not know yet: nothing tells it. In VS Code, send it a message, for example:
desk.wait.go-promote: The agent does not know yet: nothing tells it. In VS Code, send it a message, for example:
desk.go.req.test: REQ.md is confirmed. Write TEST-GUIDE.md; no plan is needed, as nothing is promoted. Then hand me the first environment.
desk.go.req.work: REQ.md is confirmed. Go on with the work; no plan is needed, as nothing is promoted.
desk.go.req: REQ.md is confirmed. Write PLAN.md, then stop for my approval.
desk.go.plan: The plan is approved. Go ahead and start.
desk.go.promote: The promote (write-back repo) is approved. Run task promote now.
desk.actions.none.hint: The agent has not stopped since your last message, so it is still working. If VS Code looks idle, answer it there.
desk.actions.new: The task is not started yet: it has no kind and no plan. Tell the agent in VS Code to open it, and this page fills in.
desk.actions.broken: The file task.json of this task is damaged, so the board cannot show the task. Restore the file from a copy; the other files of the task are not touched.
