ready.p.repos.bad.why: Some repositories cannot be used until this is mended.
ready.p.program.short: Pack {pack} cannot work yet: {programs} not found on this computer.
ready.p.program.blocked.why: The {pack} pack brings it, but the file has no permission to run. Run chmod +x on it, or ask the owner of the pack to make the package again.
ready.p.program.blocked.short: Pack {pack} cannot work yet: {programs} is there, but has no permission to run.
ready.p.cert.why: Behind the company proxy, outside addresses may fail.
ready.p.cert.short: No certificate bundle: behind the company proxy the addresses may fail.
ready.p.signin.why: The agent cannot read or write there.
ready.p.down.why: They are signed in, but the last test failed.
ready.p.skills: {n} company skills not by the rules: {names}.
ready.p.skills.one: 1 company skill not by the rules: {names}.
ready.p.noprefix: The company skills have no prefix.
ready.p.noprefix.why: Without a prefix they are not copied to the agent.
ready.p.prefix.other: The company content uses the skill prefix {wanted}; this copy uses {prefix}.
ready.p.prefix.none: The company content uses the skill prefix {wanted}; this copy has none.
ready.p.prefix.why: Nothing can be copied to the agent until the two are the same.
ready.p.prefix.short.other: The company says prefix {wanted}, this copy {prefix}: nothing is copied.
ready.p.prefix.short.none: The company says prefix {wanted}, this copy has none: nothing is copied.
ready.p.doctor: harness doctor has {n} notes about the company's content.
ready.p.doctor.one: harness doctor has 1 note about the company's content.
ready.r.setup.new: This copy is not set up.
ready.r.setup.new.why: Get ready asks for your name and language.
ready.r.setup.reopen.why: The harness command is new. Restart VS Code, so the agent finds it too.
ready.r.paired.why: Press Enter in the terminal that runs harness task board, then open the link it shows.
ready.r.vscode.wait: VS Code is not connected yet.
board.enter.vs.restart.tip: Asks VS Code to quit the normal way, waits, then opens it again with this copy's settings. A file that is not saved is asked about by VS Code.
board.enter.vs.open.tip: Opens VS Code on this copy, with this computer's settings.
board.enter.ready.nokb: Ready · not for company tasks yet
board.enter.ready.look: Ready · {n} to look at for company tasks
board.enter.cs.ok: Signed in, and the last test passed.
board.enter.cs.down: Signed in, but the last test failed.
board.vs.restart.busy.title: An agent is working
board.vs.restart.busy.one: The agent of task {name} is working. Restarting VS Code stops it.
board.vs.restart.busy: The agents of tasks {names} are working. Restarting VS Code stops them.
board.vs.restart.chat.title: A chat is still running
board.vs.restart.chat.one: A chat in VS Code is still running or waits for you: {name}. Restarting VS Code stops it.
board.vs.restart.chats: These chats in VS Code are still running or wait for you: {names}. Restarting VS Code stops them.
board.vs.restart.busy.then: VS Code may then ask you itself whether to stop them. Answer it in VS Code.
board.vs.restart.quitting: Quitting VS Code. If it asks about a file or a chat that still runs, answer it in VS Code.
board.vs.restart.opening: Opening VS Code with this copy's settings. This can take a minute.
board.vs.restart.why.still-open: VS Code did not quit. It may be asking whether to stop a chat that still runs, or whether to save a file. Look at VS Code, answer it there, then press Try again.
board.vs.restart.why.still-chat: VS Code did not quit. It may be asking whether to stop a chat that still runs ({names}), or whether to save a file. Look at VS Code, answer it there, then press Try again.
board.vs.restart.why.no-command: The board could not ask VS Code to quit. Quit it yourself, then press {@board.enter.open}.
restart.inside: This board runs in a terminal of VS Code: quitting VS Code would stop it. Start the board in a terminal outside VS Code, then try again.
restart.busy: An agent or a chat is working in: {names}.
board.ready.red.title: The agent cannot work right now
board.ready.yellow.title: Not fully ready for your company's tasks
board.ready.yellow.title.n: Not fully ready for your company's tasks: {n} to look at
desk.outbox.moved.note: The agent is not waiting for this call: it did not start a wait on it, or the wait was stopped. Dismiss it. If you still want it, approve it and tell the agent.
connections.state.nopack.tip: The tool pack of this connection is off, so there is no sign-in or test here. The gate still judges its calls by the rules of the pack: a read runs, a write is held for you, a destroy is refused.
connections.own.env.prod: No PROD here: a prod connection comes only from the company's knowledge base, and the agent only reads there.
task.step.allow_conn: The user opened these connections for this task: {names}. A write or a run on them goes through with no further approval; a destroy is still refused. Cite what you get as evidence.
task.allow.conn.on: {name} is open for this task: the agent's writes and runs on it go through with no further approval, until you close it (`harness task allow --conn {name} --off`) or the task closes. A destroy is still refused. Every call is in the log.
task.allow.conn.off: {name} is closed for this task: a write or a run on it waits for you again.
task.allow.unknown: `{name}` is not a connection. Open a connection by its name; `harness connections` lists them.
task.allow.retired: An environment is not opened any more, and `{name}` is not the name of a connection. Open one connection by its name (`harness connections` lists them), or press {open} on the card of a held call.
task.allow.no: `{name}` cannot be opened for a task: its type or your company says every write there waits for you.
gate.external.outbox.opens: The user can also open {names} for this task on the card. The wait then says opened: run the same command again, and it runs with no further approval.
serve.allow.code: Opening {name} needs the code of a held call of this task that offers it. Use the button {@desk.outbox.open} on the card of that call: press {@desk.outbox.view}, type the code, then press the button.
desk.outbox.open.tip.all: Every write and run on {name} goes through without asking you, until you close it or the task closes. A destroy is still refused. This does not approve this command. It needs the code, like {@desk.outbox.approve}.
desk.outbox.open.tip.items: Writes to the work items this task is linked to ({refs}) go through without asking you, until you close them or the task closes. Any other item, and a new item, still wait for you. This does not approve this command. It needs the code, like {@desk.outbox.approve}.
desk.outbox.opened.hint: Open for this task: {names}. The command is not approved: the agent runs it again and it goes through. One click sends that to its chat.
desk.outbox.opened.tell: Tell the agent to run it again
desk.outbox.opened.body: I opened {names} for this task. Run the same command again now, in this chat.
desk.set.open.tip.conn: For this task only. When a write or a run is held, its card has a button that opens the connection: its writes and runs then go through without asking you. A destroy is still refused; prod never opens. Linked items: a write to a ticket already linked runs without asking; a ticket newly linked, and a new ticket, still wait for you.
desk.set.open.empty: Nothing is open. When a write or a run is held, its card has a button to open the connection for this task.
desk.set.open.conn.tip: {name} is open for this task: its writes and runs go through without asking you. Click to close it again.
desk.set.open.conn.gone: {name} is not listed any more. Click to take it off this task.
desk.set.open.links.row: writes to the linked items go through ({refs})
desk.set.open.links.off.row: The items this task is linked to are not open ({refs}).
desk.set.open.links.on.tip: The linked items are open ({systems}). Click to close them again.
desk.set.open.links.off.tip: Open the linked items for this task ({systems}): a write to a ticket already linked runs without asking. Same as `harness task allow --links --on`.
board.status.open.conns: Open to the agent: {names}. Writes and runs on them go through without asking.
connections.kinds.context: Connections here: {kinds}. To find the one a task needs, run `harness connections find <words>` (a name, a system, an environment, what it is for). If you are not sure which connection or environment, ask the user; never guess.
connections.find.none: No connection fits "{words}". `harness connections` lists all {n}. If you are not sure which one the task needs, ask the user; never guess.
connections.find.empty: There is no connection here. Ask the user to set one up ({@board.enter.getready}, {@board.enter.t.connections}).
connections.find.words: Say what you look for: `harness connections find <words>`, for example the system and the environment.
connections.find.many: {n} fit. If more than one could be the one, ask the user which; never guess. Run `harness connections find` again with more words to narrow it down.
connections.find.one: One fits. When the task or the user named another environment, it is not this one: ask.
connections.find.more: {n} more fit and are not shown.
connections.named.opened: The user opened it for this task: its writes and runs go through with no further approval; a destroy is still refused.
connections.named.items: The user opened its linked items for this task: a write to one of them goes through; any other write waits for the user.
connections.first.context:
This chat reaches {names} for the first time. Its details:
{lines}
connections.own.about.ph: one line the agent finds it by, for example: sales orders, development
doctor.systems.unsigned.one: Connection {names} has no sign-in kept here, so this terminal could not reach it. Sign in to it in {@tools.conn.title} on the board, then run doctor again.
doctor.systems.unsigned: {n} connections have no sign-in kept here, so this terminal could not reach them: {names}. Sign in to them in {@tools.conn.title} on the board, then run doctor again.
ready.conn.off.one: 1 more connection has its tool pack off: {names}. It is not counted.
ready.conn.off: {n} more connections have their tool pack off: {names}. They are not counted.
setup.fact.conns.off.one: 1 more connection has its tool pack off: {names}. It is not counted.
setup.fact.conns.off: {n} more connections have their tool pack off: {names}. They are not counted.
connections.untested.tip: The sign-in is saved, but no test has reached the system yet. Press {@connections.test} when the cause is fixed: nothing needs typing again.
connections.kept: The sign-in is saved. The test did not reach the system, so it does not say the sign-in is wrong. Fix the cause above, then press {@connections.test}.
company.why.instruction.same: its copy would be {name}, the same as the copy of {other}
company.folder.error: Git could not read the folder: {error}
company.folder.unrelated: The knowledge base here and this folder do not share a history, so they cannot be joined. Nothing was changed.
company.folder.ahead: The knowledge base here has {n} commits that this folder does not have (listed below). They stay, and nothing was changed. Send them to the folder first, then update again.
company.folder.ahead.one: The knowledge base here has 1 commit that this folder does not have (listed below). It stays, and nothing was changed. Send it to the folder first, then update again.
company.folder.dirty: These files are changed here and not committed, and the update would change them too: {files}. Commit or undo them in the knowledge base first. Nothing was changed.
company.folder.same: The knowledge base here has everything this folder has. Nothing to update.
company.folder.behind: The folder has {n} commits this copy does not. The update brings in these files: {what}.
company.folder.behind.one: The folder has 1 commit this copy does not. The update brings in these files: {what}.
company.folder.uncommitted: {n} files in the folder are not committed, so they are not taken.
setup.kb.update.tick: Update the knowledge base here from this folder. What you changed here stays.
setup.kb.update.need: Tick the box to update the knowledge base.
company.folder.uncommitted.one: 1 file in the folder is not committed, so it is not taken.
setup.kb.update.stop: The update is stopped: read the note above.
board.enter.m.vscode.env: VS Code was started without this copy's settings (the tool folders and the CA bundle), so the agent's commands would run without them. Press {button}: the board opens it again with them.
board.enter.m.vscode.unseen: VS Code is open, but the board did not start it, so it cannot tell whether it has this copy's settings (the tool folders and the CA bundle). Press {button}: the board opens it again with them.
ready.r.vscode.env: VS Code was started without this copy's settings.
ready.r.vscode.unseen: VS Code was not started by the board: its settings are not known.
ready.r.vscode.env.why: The agent's commands run in it and need the tool folders and the CA bundle of this computer.
outbox.state.opened: connection opened at {at}; the agent runs the call again
gate.action.reason.bad: The reason must be one of: {reasons}.
wait.approval.none: No call with the code {code} waits for approval: the code is wrong, or the call has run, run out or was taken away. Run the command again to get a new code.
wait.approval.approved: Approved. Run exactly the same command once more now, in this session (the approval lasts {minutes} minutes).
wait.approval.opened: The user opened {names} for this task. Run exactly the same command once more now: it runs with no further approval.
wait.approval.follow.command: Change the command as the reason says (if it says nothing, ask what is wrong). The new command is held again as usual. Do not run the old one, and do not reach the same result another way.
wait.approval.follow.connection: Find the right connection or environment (`harness connections find <words>`; ask when you are not sure), then run the command for it. It is held again as usual. Do not retry this one.
wait.approval.follow.other_way: Do it the way the reason says. The gate judges the new way as usual. Do not retry this command.
wait.approval.follow.later: Stop this path and say what was not done. Do not retry, and do not reach the same result another way.
wait.approval.follow.none: Stop this path and say what was not done. Do not retry, and do not reach the same result another way.
wait.approval.timeout: No answer in {seconds} seconds. End your turn now: say which call waits (code {code}) and that the user can decide on the task page later. When they do, the board wakes you with a message. Do not run this wait again, and do not run the command yet.
wake.dismissed: I did not approve the held call {code}. Reason: {why}. {follow}
desk.outbox.reason.title: Why not?
desk.outbox.reason.tip: The agent is told your reason and does what it says. With no reason it stops that path and does nothing else.
desk.outbox.agent.wait: The agent is waiting here for your answer.
desk.outbox.agent.ended: The agent stopped on this call. Your answer wakes it.
desk.outbox.told.wait: The agent was waiting for your answer and goes on now. This card stays until the command has run (the approval lasts {minutes} minutes).
event.outbox-dismiss: the person did not approve a held call
task.finish.qa: A look closes itself: write the answer in TASK.md, then run `{command} task close --task {name}`.
task.finish.dev: The promote is the user's acceptance: after it, stop. The board closes the task when nothing else waits. Do not run `task close`, and do not ask whether to close the task.
task.finish.deliver: When the result is written and the "Done when" of REQ.md are met, write a short summary (what you delivered, where to look) and run `{command} task deliver --task {name} --summary "<text>"`, then stop. Do not ask whether to close the task: the user accepts it on the task page, or says not yet. A test where the user skipped an environment: write that it was skipped on their word, and why, in the summary and in `--skipped "<text>"`.
accept.summary.none: Give a short summary: what you delivered and where to look (`--summary "<text>"`).
accept.qa: A Q&A task closes itself when it is answered: run `{command} task close --task {name}`.
accept.promoted: This task is promoted. The promote is the user's acceptance, and the board closes the task when nothing else waits. Do not deliver it, and do not run `task close`: stop.
accept.delivered: Delivered. Say your short summary in this reply (what you delivered, where to look), then stop. The task now shows to accept on the board: the user accepts and closes it there, or says not yet in a message. Do not ask whether to close the task, and do not run `task close`.
accept.not_waiting: The task {name} is not waiting for acceptance.
accept.promote.reason: promoted: the promote is the acceptance (closed by the board)
desk.accept.hint: The agent says the work is done. Read the summary and look where it points. {@board.action.accept} writes the report and closes the task, with no message to the agent. {@desk.accept.not_yet} opens the reply box to say what is missing.
desk.accept.not_yet.tip: Opens the reply box: say what is missing, and the agent goes on.
accept.summary.file: The summary file must be a file inside the task folder ({folder}); give its path from the repository root.
event.deliver: the agent delivered the work for acceptance
task.link.suggest.open: This task names {links}. In your summary (not only in a thought), ask whether to update it now that the work is done, and what to write. Do not update it unasked. When the user says yes, draft the change with the tool pack's skill; the write waits on the task page for their approval.
setup.kb.full.here.copy: A knowledge base is already in place, and it has no git history here, so the two cannot be compared: this folder can only be put in its place as a whole.
setup.kb.update.pull.tip: The folder takes these commits from this knowledge base. Nothing in the folder is replaced. The Terminal window runs it.
setup.kb.synced.back: taken back, as they left the knowledge base: {names} (kept in .harness/runtime/company-backup/)
launch.ca.unreached.proxy: Nothing answered at the proxy {where}. Check that it runs and that the address is right.
launch.ca.unreached.host: Nothing answered at {where}. Check the address, and that this computer can reach it.
doctor.systems.why.no_answer: nothing answered: the server may be down, or this computer is off its network
doctor.systems.why.identity: the account was not let in
doctor.systems.why.exit: the probe ended with an error ({code})
doctor.systems.launch.noanswer: Check the address, the proxy and the CA bundle (Get ready, {@setup.sec.computer}); a new sign-in would not help.
desk.outbox.open.items: Open linked items of {name} for this task
desk.outbox.opened.wait: The agent was waiting for your answer and goes on now. This card stays until it has run the command again.
desk.outbox.opened.told: Told the agent. This card stays until it has run the command again.
desk.outbox.opened.asking: The agent is waiting for your answer to its question. Answer it in the chat first; after that it can run the command again.
board.enter.sys.scroll: {n} connections in all: scroll for the rest.
